lesson_title: Climate and Geomorphology Essentials: The Physical Geography Revision Sweep
hook_text: Two cyclones, one map, one glance each to tell them apart. Here is the check that never fails.
clip_script: On a synoptic map the three systems give themselves away in one glance each: a low with fronts trailing from it is the mid-latitude cyclone; a tight circular knot of isobars in the tropics without any front is the tropical cyclone; a wide letter H with lazy, spaced isobars is the anticyclone. The mid-latitude cyclone lives south of the country and drags a line of triangles for its cold front. The tropical cyclone has no fronts at all, because it is built from one warm air mass rather than two fighting ones — its isobars pack into almost perfect circles around a deep centre. Latitude, fronts, isobars. Run those three looks in order and the two storms can never be confused.
visual_style: Split-screen synoptic sketch: left, a frontal low with triangles and half-moons south of the Cape; right, a tight tropical spiral near Madagascar — a checklist stamping LATITUDE, FRONTS, ISOBARS over each in turn.
pacing: Three quick beats for the three checks, then a slow confident close on the full map.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and sweep all of physical geography's theory in one sitting.
